statements.text: I think there's no regulations around it. There's not enough. And I think this administration is not interested at all in that they have literally given them the upper hand, [allowing] the tech bros and gals of the world to do as they pleased. And we have to change that. We're going to be trying to put on an AI summit… to educate people on what it means, what jobs are at stake, how people that look like us every day in our communities [can] get involved, number one, which is a problem too.

Working people deserve innovation that expands opportunity—not eliminates it. Strengthening our understanding of how AI is impacting jobs in real time and investing directly in education makes sure Americans are not caught flat-footed as AI accelerates. [...] By prioritizing training that delivers economic gains to young people and underrepresented communities, the Workforce of the Future Act puts power back where it belongs: with the people who keep our economy running.
statements.venue: Press release on Workforce of the Future Act

statements.text: I refuse to let American workers be caught flat-footed by AI. That’s why I partnered with @repcleaver on the Workforce of the Future Act, to deliver AI training that will help workers find opportunity—putting power where it belongs: with the people. https://t.co/XU1FlFGezb
Trump recently signed an Executive Order that would overturn any State-based AI regulation deemed burdensome. What are some risks of letting AI develop unregulated?
statements.context: Opening statement at a House subcommittee hearing on quantum, AI, cloud, and cybersecurity.

statements.text: As AI data centers continue to expand, how do you balance innovation with the significant environmental and economic burdens they place on local communities and infrastructure?
statements.context: Question posed during a congressional hearing on quantum, AI, cloud, and cybersecurity.

statements.text:
Working people need to come first.

AI should create opportunities, not shrink them. Today at @homelanddems, I spoke with experts to explore how we can make sure innovation puts our communities first. https://t.co/MX9VHfPpMy

When communities are denied information, they are denied a voice. Your energy bills shouldn't skyrocket because a developer snuck an AI data center into your neighborhood without giving you the opportunity to speak out. No corporation should be able to change the fabric of a community and leave its residents to absorb the costs. That's why I'm introducing this bill to demand transparency so residents have a real say in what's happening in their community.
statements.venue: Press release on AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act

statements.text:
No one should be able to change the fabric of a community and leave its residents to absorb the costs. 

I’m introducing the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 so that you can organize and speak out when corporations try to silence your voice. https://t.co/xj3Tf09gTo

If an AI data center is being built, people should know, and be able to organize and act before the cost gets passed on to them. 

I introduced the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act last week to make sure you have a voice in your community when it comes to AI. https://t.co/WrfZdjXFWR

As we see the rise of AI data centers, residents deserve a voice in the decision-making process. 

In @HomelandDems, I discussed ways we can secure these facilities and how my new bill makes sure companies stop surprise data center construction. https://t.co/5H7XTk8jZs

Kenilworth residents are pushing back on the construction of an AI data center in their community—and I’m joining their fight. 

 I introduced a bill to stop surprise AI data center development so that residents will be notified before it’s too late to change the outcome. https://t.co/EDiJ3qo1JL

I don’t know about you, but I don’t want to cover the cost of something I didn’t order.

That’s why I introduced the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, because residents should have a voice in what happens in their neighborhood. https://t.co/1rxPnb0LSM

If we’re serious about encouraging tech innovation, we must protect the small businesses and communities that bear the costs of these changes.

In @hsbcdems, I asked the head of innovation & strategy at @kaporcenter how small businesses can use AI to assist, not replace, workers. https://t.co/xrX9ppwIe9

Artificial intelligence is often described as a tool to help small businesses become more productive and reach new customers. But its value depends entirely on the safeguards we put in place. Today's AI systems still reflect deep biases, raise serious cybersecurity risk, and operate with little transparency. While large corporations use AI to strengthen their advantage, many small businesses are left behind.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street'

statements.text: AI's rapid growth depends on the massive expansion of data centers, which place heavy burdens on local communities, local electricity grids, water supplies, infrastructure, and people, especially in my district in New Jersey's 10th. These projects often move forward with little transparency or input from the communities most effective. That is why I introduced my AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, which would bring an end to surprise AI data center construction.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street'

statements.text: While Trump is wasting money on AI air traffic control systems, Newark airport is suffering major ground delays from equipment outages. I will keep fighting for updated air traffic control infrastructure, not more AI, to keep our airports running smoothly. https://t.co/Q3zivzH1Xa
statements.quoted: An equipment outage snarled air travel, significantly delaying passengers and diverting flights. Flights at Newark, JFK and LaGuardia airports began to stack up after a contractor apparently accidentally cut 600 feet of fiber communications line. https://t.co/kOeqnIL0SH
